newsitem.title: GERMANY: German workers strike in protest of sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German workers strike in protest of sick pay.

text.p: Thousands of workers at German carmakers walked off their jobs early on Tuesday, making good on widespread threats of imminent strikes to protest cuts in sick-pay benefits that become law on October 1.
Some 7,500 workers laid down their tools at a plant in Bochum operated by Adam Opel AG, a unit of U.S.-based General Motors Corp, German television said.
Employees at Mercedes-Benz AG, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, also refused to work the night shift at a plant in Sindelfingen.

German law as of Tuesday says workers will receive 80 percent of their salaries during illnesses instead of the previous 100 percent, a pact agreed to by Bonn as part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's wide-ranging spending cuts.
Germany's powerful IG Metall metal union said on Monday it would strike even though it said that 80 percent of the workers it represents would not be affected by the change.
